correctness.rationale: Full-spark coefficient hypothesis proves smooth diagonal 4-quadric CY3 and smooth genus-17 codimension-two fixed curve. Local sign normal action gives transverse A1 quotient and a crepant blowup. Integral intersection identities for the blowup and degree-two quotient give (8,0,-32,-128). Chern integration gives e(Y)=-128; fixed-curve Euler -32 and branch-quotient formula give e(Z)=-112. Invariant rank-one H2 plus one connected exceptional component gives h11=2 and h21=58. Adjunction gives c2.E=64; descended hyperplane has six sections, KV vanishing and CY3 Riemann-Roch give c2.D=56. Simply connected quotient follows by Lefschetz plus fixed-stabilizer theorem. Standalone Python tests sample exact arithmetic; universal proof is mathematical, not finite-enumerative.

originality.rationale: The accepted statement is the specific nonfree diagonal four-quadric quotient, its smooth crepant resolution, exact cubic intersection polynomial and second-Chern pairings. The originating 2025 talk introduced these generalized-Fermat quotient questions, whereas the subsequently accessible Billi–Palomino–Sarti paper explicitly restricts its classification to fixed-point-free actions. The genus-17 curve and the Hodge pair (2,58) elsewhere are acknowledged prior art. Relevant published claims and accessible historical claims do not state or logically dominate the full decorated intersection/Chern package. This is a best-knowledge result, not proof of historical uniqueness.

value.rationale: For the naturally occurring nonfree generalized-Fermat CY3 quotient, the full marked cubic intersection and second-Chern linear data, not just a Hodge pair, are intrinsic projective numerical invariants relevant to birational/deformation comparisons and are obtained from a specific crepant model. Their geometric motivation is to understand nonfree quotient models outside the known fixed-point-free classification. The result includes singular locus and crepant resolution; a known Hodge pair alone would not meet the value bar.
